project_scope.note: The Master Plant Pool currently carries two source names for the Carolina snailseed concept. This family lesson does not resolve that species/genus taxonomy; route the duplicate-concept question to Genus Diagnostic Review.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with a woody or semi-woody twining vine with alternate simple leaves and no tendrils. Then inspect the fruit: small drupes with a single hard, strongly curved or horseshoe-shaped stone are the strongest local family confirmation.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Climbing vines; leaves alternate, simple, petiolate, often broadly ovate to cordate or shallowly lobed, with several strong veins arising near the leaf base; tendrils absent.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers small and inconspicuous, typically unisexual; parts are separate rather than forming a showy fused corolla. Family-level confirmation is easier from fruit/stone than flower color.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A drupe with one hard endocarp; the curved moon/snail-shaped stone is the key teaching structure.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: If the plant is climbing, first ask whether it has tendrils. No tendrils + alternate broad leaves + clusters of drupes with a curved stone points toward Menispermaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: vine habit → node/tendril check → leaf venation → fruit cluster → stone/endocarp
visual_lesson.intro: The fastest local recognition route is to stop treating every vine as a tendril-climber. Menispermaceae twines with the stem itself, then confirms with a distinctive one-seeded drupe and curved stone.

steps.title: 1 · Check the climbing mechanism
steps.look_for: Stem wrapping around support; no axillary or leaf-opposed tendril.
steps.why_it_matters: Immediately separates the local lesson from Vitaceae, Passifloraceae and Cucurbitaceae.

steps.title: 2 · Read the leaf base and veins
steps.look_for: Alternate simple blade with several strong basal veins, often cordate/ovate.
steps.why_it_matters: Useful vegetative support, but not enough alone.

steps.title: 3 · Follow the fruit to the stone
steps.look_for: Small drupe surrounding one hard curved/horseshoe-shaped endocarp.
steps.why_it_matters: The endocarp is the strongest family-level visual lock.

comparisons.title: Menispermaceae vs Vitaceae
comparisons.rule: Vitaceae usually climbs with tendrils opposite leaves and makes multi-seeded berries; Menispermaceae twines without tendrils and has a one-stoned drupe.

comparisons.title: Menispermaceae vs Passifloraceae
comparisons.rule: Passiflora has axillary tendrils and conspicuous corona-bearing flowers; Menispermaceae lacks tendrils and confirms with the hard curved drupe stone.

comparisons.title: Menispermaceae vs Convolvulaceae
comparisons.rule: Both may twine without obvious tendrils, but Convolvulaceae has a fused funnel/salverform corolla and capsule; Menispermaceae has tiny flowers and drupes with a hard curved stone.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not use the current Cocculus carolinus / Nephroia carolina source-name duplication to teach two local species until Genus Diagnostic Review resolves the accepted concept.
